subject: research/capture-stereodepth
professional: a senior computer-vision researcher in dense stereo and depth-image-based rendering (the reviewer a CVPR/3DV or IEEE TIP paper on stereo-for-view-synthesis would get). They would check first that disparity = f*B/z is implemented right, that the matcher is scored with standard Middlebury/KITTI metrics on non-occluded pixels, whether the baseline sweep sits in a sane disparity range, how holes are scored in the warp, and whether 'correlated errors' is separated from 'missing depth' before it is named as the cause.

Independent script /tmp/claude-0/sd/scripts/indep.py (run with `-I`, OpenCV 5.1 installed to /tmp/claude-0/sd/pylib). (1) Focal length by hand 96/tan(30 deg) = 166.277 px = code F; disparity at z=3 m, B=0.2 m = 11.085 px. (2) An auditor-written naive 7x7 SAD winner-take-all on a synthetic random pattern shifted by 7.0 px gives median 7.0; project match() gives 7.000 with 100% LR-check pass; at a 7.4 px shift match() gives 7.27 (parabola pixel-locking bias, see domain). (3) Ground-truth disparity F*B/lz with an auditor occlusion mask by reprojection into the right view: project BM non-occluded EPE 0.265 / 0.294 / 0.445 px and bad-1px 3.4 / 4.3 / 6.8% at B = 3 / 20 / 50 cm; mean relative depth error on its valid pixels 15.25 / 4.51 / 2.85% for seed 0, consistent with results.txt means 14.87 / 4.29 / 2.72 over 3 seeds. (4) sigma = mean|e|*sqrt(pi/2) for a Gaussian with that mean absolute error: Monte Carlo 0.03988 vs hand 0.03989. Every README table number traces to results.txt. The arithmetic is right; what the numbers are said to mean is the problem (claims, domain). 3.

evidence.craft: Read scene.py (107 lines), stereo.py (64), synth.py (75), run.py, figure.py, tests. Vectorised numpy, summed-area box filter, deterministic seeds, the right-reference cost re-indexed from the left volume rather than recomputed (correct: cr[d, y, x] = cl[d, y, x + d]). Defects: scene.py and synth.py are copied from capture-novelview and have since diverged (novelview's synth.py now has fill_holes and hole_fraction; this copy paints holes sky blue only); `from .scene import pixel_rays` inside warp() (synth.py:16) though the module already imports from .scene; magic cost 3.0 for out-of-range columns repeated three times (stereo.py:21,24,47); right depth returned and discarded (run.py:22); stale runtime in run.py:3. 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: every table number in README:27-41 matches results.txt; 7 tests; 'iid scores 1.2 to 7.3 dB better' (20.83-13.51 = 7.32, 23.45-22.29 = 1.16); '2.5 dB below the nearest camera' (24.81-22.29); bystander '3 to 4 dB below' (3.74, 3.30); limitations and AI disclosure present. NOT backed: (a) the headline 'the synthesised in-between view ... never beats cutting to the nearest camera' (README:3, 38) holds only because holes are painted sky blue; with capture-novelview's own nearest-camera hole fill (its README calls it 'the simplest fallback a depth-image-based renderer uses') measured stereo depth scores 27.12 / 27.19 / 27.58 dB at B = 10 / 20 / 30 cm against 24.82 for the nearest camera and 27.29 exact (/tmp/claude-0/sd/scripts/fill.py). The README never says holes are painted sky. (b) 'optimistic ... because stereo errors are correlated and missing depth leaves holes' (README:3, 39): giving the iid model the same hole mask gives 13.98 dB at 3 cm (measured 13.56) and 21.85 at 20 cm (measured 22.25), so holes explain essentially all of the gap and correlated errors none (indep.py section 5). (c) 'Semi-global matching ... would raise every number' (README:45) is asserted, not tested; one OpenCV SGBM configuration gave lower coverage (0.736 vs 0.902 at 20 cm) and similar error. 1.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on it, and research/capture-hybrid did (and reversed the headline with hole filling and an LR-disagreement gate, 29.2 dB). Nearest prior work: the baseline/accuracy/occlusion trade-off is textbook (dz = z^2 dd / (f B); Okutomi and Kanade, 'A multiple-baseline stereo', IEEE TPAMI 1993); SGM (Hirschmueller, TPAMI 2008); Middlebury and KITTI evaluation protocols; DIBR and its hole problem (Fehn 2004) and the effect of depth errors on synthesised views (Merkle et al. 2009, depth-coding for view synthesis). Only Scharstein and Szeliski 2002 is cited. 'Error falls with baseline, coverage does not' restates the multi-baseline motivation; the new part, the PSNR comparison, is an artefact of the hole policy. 2.
evidence.domain: Against Middlebury/KITTI practice: no standard disparity metrics are reported (EPE, bad-1/bad-2 px, D1) though ground-truth disparity is available from F*B/lz; the auditor's numbers show the matcher is in fact good (EPE 0.27-0.45 px non-occluded), which mean relative depth error hides. The 3 cm row is degenerate: true disparity on the whole surface is at most 1.9 px and 40.4% of surface pixels are under 1 px, so its 55% coverage is the min_disp rule, not stereo failure. At 50 cm the coverage loss is mostly the left field-of-view strip without overlap (10.2% of surface) rather than occlusion as README:38 says. Sub-pixel parabola on SAD has the known pixel-locking bias (true 7.1 / 7.25 / 7.4 -> 7.03 / 7.11 / 7.27; equiangular fit, Shimizu and Okutomi 2005, gives 7.06 / 7.18 / 7.35), which matters most at 1-2 px disparity. The LR check and WTA follow Scharstein-Szeliski correctly, and parallel-axis rendering makes rectification exact (disclosed). 2.

defects.what: Headline 'the synthesised in-between view ... never beats cutting to the nearest camera' is an artefact of painting holes sky blue (synth.py:59), which the README never states. With the parent project's own nearest-camera hole fill, measured stereo depth scores 27.1-27.6 dB at 10-30 cm against 24.8 for the nearest camera and 27.3 exact, so the conclusion reverses (research/capture-hybrid later found the same).

'The assumed noise model is optimistic ... because stereo errors are correlated and missing depth leaves holes': giving the iid model the same hole mask closes the gap (13.98 vs 13.56 dB at 3 cm; 21.85 vs 22.25 at 20 cm), so holes explain it and correlated errors do not; the two causes were never separated.

No standard stereo metrics (EPE, bad-pixel %, KITTI D1, non-occluded mask) though ground-truth disparity is available; mean relative depth error hides that the matcher is sub-pixel accurate (EPE 0.27-0.45 px).

The 3 cm baseline row is degenerate: true disparity is at most 1.9 px and 40% of surface pixels fall under the 1 px floor, so its 55% coverage and 14.9% error measure the min_disp cut and quantisation, not stereo; at 50 cm most lost coverage is the no-overlap left strip, not occlusion as README:38 says.
synth.py (every PSNR in the headline) has no test, and the left-right check is unpinned: 4 of 7 seeded mutants survive (LR check disabled, z-buffer reversed, crack fill, iid sigma).
'Semi-global matching ... would raise every number' is asserted; one OpenCV SGBM configuration lowered coverage (0.74 vs 0.90 at 20 cm) with similar error.

Prior work not cited: multi-baseline stereo (Okutomi and Kanade 1993), SGM (Hirschmueller 2008), DIBR holes (Fehn 2004), depth error effects on synthesised views (Merkle et al. 2009); the error-vs-baseline trade-off is textbook dz = z^2 dd / (f B).
Parabola sub-pixel fit on SAD costs has pixel-locking bias (7.4 px -> 7.27; equiangular fit gives 7.35), largest where disparities are 1-2 px.
scene.py and synth.py are copies of capture-novelview that have diverged (no fill_holes or hole_fraction here); import inside warp(); magic cost 3.0 repeated.
run.py docstring says 'about a minute'; it runs in 12 s (README says 10 s). Next steps list a hole filler and LR confidence fallback that research/capture-hybrid has since built, unlinked.

verdict: A compact, deterministic and reproducible stereo-to-view-synthesis pipeline: results.txt rebuilds byte for byte in 12 s, the focal length and disparity geometry check by hand, and against ground-truth disparity the block matcher is good (non-occluded EPE 0.27-0.45 px, bad-1px 3-7%). It does not meet the bar. The headline, that view synthesis from measured depth never beats cutting to the nearest camera, comes from painting holes sky blue: with the parent project's own nearest-camera hole fill, measured depth reaches 27.2 dB against 24.8 for cutting and 27.3 for exact depth. The stated cause of the iid model's optimism (correlated errors) disappears once the iid model gets the same holes. The 3 cm row sits below a 2 px disparity range. Standard stereo metrics are absent, synth.py is untested and 4 of 7 seeded mutants survive. A dense-stereo reviewer would accept the matcher but not the conclusion.
